claims.statement: Airtable issues OAuth access tokens after a user authorizes a registered OAuth integration; they are passed as a bearer token and expire after an expected 60 minutes.

sources.supports: The OAuth access tokens you receive should be passed with your API requests as a `Authorization: Bearer header`.
`access_token` | An opaque string. Can be used to make requests to the Airtable API on behalf of the user, and cannot be recovered if lost.

claims.statement: Airtable states that OAuth access and refresh tokens are opaque, variable-length strings with no reliance on a particular length or format.

sources.supports: OAuth access and refresh tokens should be treated as opaque, variable-length strings. In particular, do not rely on tokens having a particular length or format.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: No prefix, alphabet or length is stated for OAuth access tokens and the provider says not to rely on any; the candidate is not researched beyond existence. Lead only: one scanner detector artifact by a single maintainer (trufflesecurity/trufflehog @ 59e3b04e820c4cad30462696ac497853a5f7679c, pkg/detectors/airtableoauth/airtableoauth.go L28) uses a pattern with ".v1." separators; a single artifact does not meet the tool-corroborated requirement, so no format claim is recorded.
